parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
of the earth means belonging to the land rather than the sea

explanation.surface: A question about what makes the best kind of landlubber sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is read in answer order: a sailor (SALT) 'of land' (OF THE EARTH), the land-sailor of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from the Gospels describes thoroughly good, decent people, the best of humankind.

explanation.surface: A generous person who also writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-handed is a free spender of money; Stephen Spender was an English poet of the 1930s generation.

clue.text: Italian genius can overdo inlaid design

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new design, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian master might overdo his inlaid decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' is the anagram signal on all fifteen letters of 'can overdo inlaid'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance painter, inventor and anatomist is the classic example of a universal genius from Italy.

clue.text: Roman author of "The Moon and Sixpence"?

parts.note: a full moon is round, the shape of the letter O
six is VI in Roman numerals and D is the old abbreviation for a penny (denarius)

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Roman wrote Maugham's novel The Moon and Sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface names Somerset Maugham's novel, but the title is wordplay: a round moon O, then six (VI) and penny (D, pre-1971 British money).
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Ovidius Naso wrote the Metamorphoses and the Ars Amatoria in Augustan Rome.

explanation.surface: A sentimental gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means soft-hearted or loving; to tender is to offer or put forward formally, as with a resignation.

definitions.note: the possessive reads as 'shipper is', with the definition as a noun

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
porter is a dark beer, a close relative of stout

explanation.surface: A shipping merchant's ex-wife is plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like a description of the wife, but it is the dark beer PORTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that sends goods abroad by sea is a shipper of them.

parts.note: Jack is a sailor (Jack Tar), and the senior rating in the navy is the seaman described by this fitness word

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is as healthy as a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a crossword sailor; an AB is an able-bodied seaman, so the word for fitness is also his rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Being physically strong and healthy describes the condition, and the able seaman rank takes its name from it.

parts.note: the emblem of the Isle of Man is the triskelion, three legs joined at the hip
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A school sports-day event put on for Isle of Man folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The flag of the Isle of Man (Manx) shows three armoured legs, so Manx people are a 'three-legged race'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pairs tie their adjoining legs together and hobble to the finish in this comic school sports event.

parts.note: drawers are not chest furniture but people drawing on pipes and cigarettes, in a railway carriage set aside for them

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture with drawers built in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' suggests a chest of drawers; here they are people who draw on cigarettes, in the old railway carriage where tobacco was allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains once had a carriage or compartment set aside for passengers who wished to light up.

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
motion is movement or flow

explanation.surface: Flowing energy generates heat, a physics statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmth' reads as heat from physics, but it is warmth of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth of feeling is a strong sentiment, as when one is moved by something.

explanation.surface: A man named Palmer described as forward-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmer was a medieval traveller to the Holy Land carrying a palm leaf; Bunyan's Christian is the traveller of The Pilgrim's Progress.

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the word for poet is read backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet; the possessive gives the word whose retirement follows

explanation.surface: Plain grey fabric chosen for a writer's quiet old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' means the poet's word BARD is drawn back, read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab is a dull light-brown or grey woollen or cotton fabric, the source of the adjective for dull.

clue.text: The ark-bear suffering such intense grief

indicators.note: the letters are in a suffering, troubled state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bear on Noah's ark suffering terrible sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' is the anagram signal on the ten letters of 'The ark-bear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelming sorrow, especially after lost love, is the feeling of a shattered heart.

parts.note: Noah's great deluge is pictured as a lamp he turned on

explanation.surface: Asks whether Noah turned on a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: A strong lamp lighting a stadium is read as the light that brought on the Flood, the deluge of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful lamp for lighting a building or stadium at night is switched on like any electric light.

indicators.note: the word for tour goes around the letters that follow

parts.note: a ride is a trip or tour

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, the first and last letters of the Irish county name

explanation.surface: A mystery coach tour around the edge of County Donegal in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts DL, the first and last letters of Donegal, inside RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question or enigma is a conundrum whose answer is hidden.

clue.text: Principal equipment of bowlers, for example

parts.note: the head is the principal of a school
gear is kit or equipment

explanation.surface: The chief kit used by cricket bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowlers' look like cricketers; they are bowler hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowler hats are an example of things worn on the head.

clue.text: One willing to try a hill

parts.note: to test is to try
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone happy to have a go at climbing a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' looks like eagerness; it is making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so one who is willing in that legal sense.

clue.text: Low-down at spa hotel is a gas!

parts.note: a hydro is a hotel offering water treatments, a spa hotel
gen is slang for information, the low-down

explanation.surface: Gossip heard at a spa hotel is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gas' reads as slang for great fun; it is a chemical gas. The charade is in answer order, the low-down GEN placed 'at' (after) HYDRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element, a colourless flammable gas.

clue.text: To this matter, it could be three-love

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the round zero O

explanation.surface: A tennis scoreline of three-love relevant to this matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' signals an anagram of THREE, then 'love' gives O, the zero of tennis scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal legal word meaning to this document or concerning this point.

parts.note: H is the map sign and abbreviation for hospital
an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A distinguished member of a hospital team.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is the eight-oar rowing crew, as in the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a high point or elevated ground, a rise in the land.

indicators.note: embracing is holding within, so the word for attempt goes round the next piece

aged means old

explanation.surface: Trying to welcome old age in hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts AGED inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a disaster or great misfortune, a calamity that brings hardship.

indicators.note: only the start of the name is kept, the first name and the first letter of the surname

parts.note: Puck of A Midsummer Night's Dream is also called Robin Goodfellow

explanation.surface: Puck from Shakespeare being dressed, with only his upper half clothed.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck's other name is Robin Goodfellow; keeping only its top, ROBIN plus G, leaves the answer.

clue.text: Uncertain line a voter demonstrates in such disclosure

explanation.surface: An undecided voter shows his hand in what he reveals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncertain' is the anagram signal on the ten letters of 'line a voter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprising disclosure or uncovering of something secret makes things known.

explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim, a thought that comes to mind.

clue.text: Toddler near tucked in later today

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh means near

explanation.surface: A toddler close by, tucked into bed later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked in' puts NIGH inside TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening, later on the same day, is when the night comes.

clue.text: Cut off or loosen tie, also

indicators.note: loosening the letters frees them to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to cut off or loosen a necktie as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosen' is the anagram signal on 'tie also'.

clue.text: Imagine number of spec taters the Tate, for example

parts.note: to picture something is to imagine it
the gallery is the crowd of spectators watching, as at a golf tournament

explanation.surface: Picture a crowd of people viewing the Tate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art museums in London and elsewhere in Britain; 'spec taters' is the newspaper's line break in 'spectators'.
